variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Tokenization is the versioned process that turns text into a sequence of integer token IDs. A token can represent a word, part of a word, punctuation, whitespace, a byte sequence, or a control marker.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Follow text through the tokenizer pipeline”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Normalize text
pairs.detail: Preserve the input or apply a declared transformation such as NFC, NFKC, case folding, or accent handling.
pairs.explanation: Preserve the input or apply a declared transformation such as NFC, NFKC, case folding, or accent handling. This step can change code points and offsets.

pairs.label: Expose boundaries
pairs.detail: Mark candidate regions such as whitespace, punctuation, digits, or raw bytes.
pairs.explanation: Mark candidate regions such as whitespace, punctuation, digits, or raw bytes. These are candidates, not necessarily final tokens.

pairs.label: Choose vocabulary pieces
pairs.detail: Apply learned BPE merge ranks, WordPiece rules, or unigram scores to select pieces that exist in the fixed vocabulary.
pairs.explanation: Apply learned BPE merge ranks, WordPiece rules, or unigram scores to select pieces that exist in the fixed vocabulary.

pairs.label: Insert model structure
pairs.detail: Add trusted beginning, ending, separator, role, or padding IDs and produce masks, type IDs, and offsets expected by the model.
pairs.explanation: Add trusted beginning, ending, separator, role, or padding IDs and produce masks, type IDs, and offsets expected by the model.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. A tokenizer and a model checkpoint form one contract.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Tokenization is the versioned process that turns text into a sequence of integer token IDs. A token can represent a word, part of a word, punctuation, whitespace, a byte sequence, or a control marker.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Distinguish vocabulary learning from runtime segmentation”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: BPE-style merging
pairs.detail: Begin with small symbols, often characters or bytes, then learn ranked merges for adjacent pairs that occur frequently.
pairs.explanation: Begin with small symbols, often characters or bytes, then learn ranked merges for adjacent pairs that occur frequently. At runtime, applicable merges combine symbols according to the saved rules. A larger merge vocabulary often shortens common sequences but spends capacity on the training corpus's frequent patterns.

pairs.label: Unigram segmentation
pairs.detail: Begin with many candidate pieces, assign probabilities, and remove pieces while preserving likely segmentations.
pairs.explanation: Begin with many candidate pieces, assign probabilities, and remove pieces while preserving likely segmentations. At runtime, dynamic programming finds a high-scoring path through possible pieces. Multiple valid paths can exist, which also enables subword sampling during training.

pairs.label: WordPiece behavior
pairs.detail: WordPiece also builds subword units but uses its own training and continuation-marker conventions.
pairs.explanation: WordPiece also builds subword units but uses its own training and continuation-marker conventions. Similar-looking token strings do not imply identical IDs, normalization, unknown-token handling, or segmentation.

pairs.label: Byte or unknown fallback
pairs.detail: Byte-backed vocabularies can represent arbitrary UTF-8 input without one global unknown token, though rare scripts may expand into many tokens.
pairs.explanation: Byte-backed vocabularies can represent arbitrary UTF-8 input without one global unknown token, though rare scripts may expand into many tokens. Other tokenizers may emit an unknown token when no allowed piece covers a span.

pairs.label: Coverage slices

pairs.label: Task regressions

pairs.explanation: Run downstream quality and safety evaluations. A tokenizer can reduce sequence length while damaging labels, code completion, retrieval spans, or generation behavior.

pairs.label: Release evidence

pairs.explanation: Record corpus version, tokenizer artifacts, library version, hashes, metrics, approval, and rollback target. Compare candidates on the same frozen evaluation set.

variants.prompt: Why does a language model consume token IDs instead of token spellings?
options: Each ID selects a learned row from the model's embedding table
Integer IDs automatically verify the text
IDs remove the need for positional information
Every ID has the same meaning across tokenizers
variants.explanation: The tokenizer-model contract maps each ID to one learned embedding row. The same integer can mean something entirely different in another vocabulary.

variants.prompt: What can NFC normalization change for a decomposed sequence such as e plus a combining acute accent?
options: It can compose the sequence, changing bytes and later offsets
It always translates the text into English
It adds a beginning-of-sequence token
It guarantees fewer tokens for every tokenizer
variants.explanation: NFC can replace canonically equivalent decomposed sequences with precomposed code points. Segmentation may then change, but a lower token count is not guaranteed.
